title: Why are African Laborers so JACKED?
summary: NH asks why some African laborers, such as Cameroonian sand divers and gold miners, look so muscular. He says genetics are only part of it: heavy, high-volume daily labor that never goes to failure, natural selection in brutal jobs, and year-round leanness from scarce food do most of the work. He ends by stressing mindset and environment over genetics.
claims: People are not born equal for muscle building; some gain in 1 year what takes others 10, but that is no excuse to skip the gym
The idea that all Black men are gifted for muscle is an overgeneralization: there are plenty of skinny-fat Black men, and traits that help in sprinting hurt in swimming
Proposed reasons for a muscle-building edge in men of African descent are higher average testosterone and growth hormone and fast-twitch fiber dominance
The body adapts to its sport, so sprinters look muscular and marathoners slim
Sub-Saharan Africa is a land of very different tribes (for example Hutu versus Tutsi), and men who look jacked without training are outliers even in countries like Cameroon, Nigeria or Senegal
Most manual laborers, African or Western, are not jacked: many African miners are lean and wiry, and construction workers tend to be strong but fat
Cameroonian sand divers on the Wouri river dive about 20 feet and walk out along the riverbed carrying buckets hundreds of times a day, a sort of loaded carry underwater
Each filled sand bucket weighs about 18 kg (40 lb) and must be lifted overhead into the boat; with bailing water and pushing boats against strong currents, the job trains the whole body
The divers' work resembles 'nucleus overload': huge frequent volume with tiny load increases and never going to failure, and it still builds muscle over years because fatigue adds up
Cameroonian gold miners swing pickaxes and carry rock for up to 12 hours a day; Francis Ngannou did this work
Natural selection shapes these jobs: those who cannot handle the work quit, and the survivors end up muscular
Few European workers look this way because developed nations hand heavy labor to machines; ten years of hauling sand would make most people muscular
Necessity drives effort: for these men losing the job can mean starvation, a level of motivation few gym-goers have
They look jacked partly because they are lean year-round, with no access to a caloric surplus and a mostly low-calorie whole-food diet; an aesthetic physique is first of all a lean one
Hunter tribesmen stay fit from daily hunting but never reach the physique that regular resistance training produces
African lifters training in community-owned gyms with scrap-metal equipment and limited food still build exceptional physiques, which shows mindset matters more than equipment
Mindset and environment decide success more than genetics; these same men raised in a comfortable Western country would probably never be called genetically gifted
